subject: Order Form — capacity redistribution & SLA band adjustment (redlines)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@catalystlabs.ai>
Cc: procurement@catalystlabs.ai
Date: 2026-09-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form — capacity redistribution & SLA band adjustment (redlines)

Hi Alyssa,

Attached is our proposed redline to the Order Form (Catalyst_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). Summary of the commercial changes we discussed on the call:

- Reallocate 20% of Reserved GPU nodes into the Burst Pool (exposure window: Q4 pilot).
- Introduce an SLA "band" for burst traffic: 95% of requests remain under 150ms for reserved pool; burst pool carries a 99th percentile credit structure.
- Billing/proration: fees are prorated on a daily basis for mid-month capacity changes (draft language in attachment).
- SOW: add brief observability appendix for per-route latency dashboards and 12-month audit logs.

Please review the redlines and flag any commercial or legal blockers. If these look good, our plan is to convert to an amendment (one-page) and route via DocuSign.

Key asks for Catalyst: confirm whether you want the Burst Pool to be charged at a premium flat multiplier (we proposed 1.25x) or on a per-token basis. Also confirm internal procurement timeline so we can align implementation milestones.

Attaching: Catalyst_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf, SOW-Appendix-Observability-diff.docx

Thanks,
Connor

On Tue, Sep 28, 2026 at 9:15 AM Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attached is our proposed redline to the Order Form (Catalyst_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). Summary of the commercial changes we discussed on the call:
>
> - Reallocate 20% of Reserved GPU nodes into the Burst Pool (exposure window: Q4 pilot).
> - Introduce an SLA "band" for burst traffic: 95% of requests remain under 150ms for reserved pool; burst pool carries a 99th percentile credit structure.
> - Billing/proration: fees are prorated on a daily basis for mid-month capacity changes (draft language in attachment).
> - SOW: add brief observability appendix for per-route latency dashboards and 12-month audit logs.
>

Thanks, Connor. Quick clarifying questions from procurement/legal so we can triage internally:

1) Billing/proration: can you confirm the exact formula you propose for daily proration? Our finance team needs the arithmetic for our ERP.
2) SLA credits: what triggers a credit for the burst pool vs reserved pool? If burst pool is best-effort, we need clear language to avoid disputes.
3) Observability SOW: we like the idea but need the acceptance criteria for the dashboards and whether Redwood will host any of this data.
4) Implementation timeline: can you provide a mutually agreed M-A-P (mutual action plan) with dates for signing, provisioning, and acceptance?

We attached our procurement checklist internally — we can run a legal redline in parallel but will need explicit amendment language for the MSA/Order Form rather than inline notes.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Cloud Ops | Catalyst Labs
alyssa.chen@catalystlabs.ai

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@catalystlabs.ai>, procurement@catalystlabs.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order Form — capacity redistribution & SLA band adjustment (redlines)

Looping in Laura (legal) and Aditya (finance) to help resolve Alyssa's questions. Key items to cover:

- Provide exact proration formula for mid-month capacity adjustments (finance needs precise wording to feed ERP).
- SLA credit triggers: define distinct triggers for reserved pool vs burst pool; recommend "reserved pool SLA applies to pinned capacity; burst pool is best-effort but carries a different SLA credit at 99th pctl measured over a monthly window."
- Observability SOW acceptance criteria: propose an Acceptance Checklist in Appendix A (list of 6 functional checks + synthetic load test).

Attachments: Catalyst_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf (original), SOW-Appendix-Observability-diff.docx (proposed language).

If legal can draft a short amendment (one page) and a clean redline we'll send to Alyssa with a DocuSign link. Aditya — if finance can confirm the proration formula and the suggested 1.25x burst multiplier commercially, I'll include that in the amendment.

Connor

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@catalystlabs.ai>, procurement@catalystlabs.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — capacity redistribution & SLA band adjustment (redlines)

Connor — thanks for the ping. I reviewed the redlines and propose the following (high level):

1) Proration language: replace "fees are prorated on a daily basis" with "Fees will be prorated on a pro rata daily basis calculated as (monthly committed fee / number of days in the calendar month) x number of days in effect." This gives finance the arithmetic they need.

2) SLA credit triggers: define two discrete metrics in the Order Form: (a) Reserved pool: availability measured per calendar month; credits calculated as % of monthly fee up to a capped amount; (b) Burst pool: qualify as "best-effort" with explicit non-guarantee of latency, but include a separate credit table for specific 99th percentile outage definitions so we have an SLA metric to refer to (prevents no-SLA disputes).

3) Amendment vs inline redline: recommend we prepare a one-page Amendment to the MSA that: (i) describes the capacity redistribution; (ii) attaches the Order Form as amended; (iii) confirms observability Appendix A; and (iv) preserves audit log retention for 12 months.

4) Acceptance and implementation: add an "Implementation Acceptance" clause to SOW Appendix A with staged milestones (Provisioning, Smoke Test, Performance Acceptance) and a 7-business-day remedy/rollback window following each milestone.

5) Commercial note: if Catalyst accepts the 1.25x burst multiplier, we should confirm with Finance on any minimum fee adjustments. Aditya, please advise if a 1.25x multiplier needs VP approval or if it's within quota.

I'll draft AMENDMENT-draft-connor.docx with the suggested language and return a redline by EOD. Connor, once you have Aditya's confirmation on the multiplier I'll finalize and we can route to Alyssa as a DocuSign envelope.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-01T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form — capacity redistribution & SLA band adjustment (redlines)

Alyssa — thanks for the quick turnaround. Next actionable steps below so we don't get blocked:

Mutual action plan (proposed):
- Oct 1: Redwood legal delivers draft amendment (attached: AMENDMENT-draft-connor.docx).
- Oct 4: Catalyst legal to review and provide counter-comments.
- Oct 6: Commercial sign-off (both parties) and DocuSign route.
- Oct 13: Provisioning window opens / provisioning complete by Oct 15.
- Oct 18: Performance Acceptance (synthetic checks) and go-live for burst pilot.

Aditya has confirmed the 1.25x burst multiplier is acceptable for typical deals within the current quota; he will confirm any executive approval required if Catalyst requests a lower multiplier. Laura, please mark any final edits on the amendment and I will send the DocuSign link once Catalyst confirms Oct 6 sign-off target.

Alyssa — please confirm whether the MAP dates above work for you and whether Catalyst prefers a flat multiplier or itemized per-token billing for burst usage. If you confirm the MAP, we'll circulate the DocuSign envelope and associated amendment redline.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
